br-1lVl.title: Plate: white with blue top stripe, red commercial
br-1lVl.summary: Plates were white until 2018. Now they are white with a blue stripe on top. Commercial vehicles still use red plates.

br-2B6I.title: Road lines: double yellow centre, white edges
br-2B6I.summary: Double yellow centre lines with white edge lines. Narrow roads sometimes have a single dashed yellow line.

br-2DzR.title: Streetlight: lamp arm curved all the way
br-2DzR.summary: In Rio de Janeiro, lamp arms are curved along their whole length, not seen anywhere else.

br-3Oaz.title: Insulator: spool-of-thread shape
br-3Oaz.summary: Spool-of-thread insulators are mostly in Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo, and have been seen in Ceará.

br-3Pyz.title: Road: cobblestone pavement
br-3Pyz.summary: Cobblestone pavement is most common in the Northeast and Rio Grande do Sul.

br-3jxg.title: Landscape: highest mountains near the south-east
br-3jxg.summary: Elevation map: the highest mountains are near the south-east coast. Learn which regions are flat.

br-5M2t.title: Streetlight: blue with orange arm
br-5M2t.summary: Lamps in Teresina (Piauí) are usually blue with an orange arm.

br-5T9U.title: Insulator: transparent
br-5T9U.summary: Transparent insulators are mostly in Alagoas and Santa Catarina, and rarely in Sergipe, Ceará and Brasília.

br-6UVb.title: Plants: coffee
br-6UVb.summary: Coffee is by far most common in Minas Gerais, but also in Espírito Santo and north-eastern São Paulo.

br-6VbT.title: Google car: smudge at front right, blue stripe
br-6VbT.summary: In all newer Gen 4 coverage in Amapá, the front right of the camera is smudged and the car is white with a blue stripe.

br-6v5Y.title: Pole: lopsided crossbar with support to its middle
br-6v5Y.summary: A lopsided crossbar with a support reaching the middle of the longer arm. Most common in São Paulo; frequent in Rio Grande do Sul, Rio de Janeiro and Mato Grosso do Sul.

br-8AoE.title: Road: white painted kerbs
br-8AoE.summary: White painted kerbs are common on roads.

br-90g6.title: Streetlight: white numbered plaque on the lamp
br-90g6.summary: Newer Gen 4 lamps in Belo Horizonte and Uberaba (Minas Gerais) can have a white numbered plaque: starting 0 or 1 in Belo Horizonte, 1 or 2 in Uberaba.

br-AThg.title: Sign: street name stickers wrapped around poles
br-AThg.summary: Street signs in Campo Grande and Joinville are stickers wrapped around a pole at junctions. Campo Grande ones usually carry extra info and a red and yellow stripe.

br-B0KY.title: Road: green rainforest, orange soil, mostly unpaved
br-B0KY.summary: Road 319 in Amazonas: flat and mostly unpaved through bright green rainforest with bright orange soil, paved near Manaus. Wooden or ladder poles all along. Blue Gen 4 car.

br-BAUZ.title: Road: lots of divided highways
br-BAUZ.summary: São Paulo has far more divided highways than any other state.

br-BSvK.title: Landscape: dry mountains with many folds
br-BSvK.summary: Near Uiramutã in northern Roraima: a dry landscape with large mountains full of folds.

br-BuMI.title: Landscape: dense rainforest
br-BuMI.summary: The Amazon is dense rainforest covering 40% of the country. The few roads go through rich forest or grassy hills with few trees.

br-CDnw.title: Pole: black double-UFO insulators in a trident
br-CDnw.summary: Black double UFO-shaped insulators in a trident layout are common in Maranhão. The insulator is common elsewhere, but not in this layout.

br-CZb8.title: Pole: smooth cone on top (pencil pole)
br-CZb8.summary: Poles with a smooth cone on top like a pencil: common in Rio de Janeiro, rare in Brasília and Manaus.

br-CeyJ.title: Road: hilly, curvy, dry, busy with trucks
br-CeyJ.summary: The Pará stretch of road 163: hilly, curvy, dry and sometimes hazy, with varied Amazon plants and lots of trucks. Blue Gen 4 car in the north, low small-camera car in the south.

br-Cwjn.title: Satellite dish: transparent
br-Cwjn.summary: Transparent satellite dishes are fairly common and generally unique to this country in Latin America.

br-DS2b.title: Insulator: long grey (not horizontal)
br-DS2b.summary: Long grey insulators (not horizontal) are most common in Pará, Mato Grosso, Tocantins, Bahia, Mato Grosso do Sul, Paraná and Santa Catarina; rare in Maranhão, Rio Grande do Norte, Alagoas, Sergipe, Rondônia and Rio Grande do Sul.

br-Dz8D.title: Plants: eucalyptus plantations
br-Dz8D.summary: Very tall eucalyptus in big or small plantations or growing anywhere. Seen all over the south, with some large plantations in Amapá too.

br-FOZn.title: Plants: coconut palms
br-FOZn.summary: Tall coconut palms with long leaves and thin trunks, common in the Northeast states and sometimes further west or south along the coast. They grow worldwide.

br-GV3p.title: Coverage: boat and walking camera on Amazon rivers
br-GV3p.summary: In Amazonas and Mato Grosso: boat and walking coverage on and near the Madeira and Aripuanã rivers, south of road 319, through dense rainforest and small villages.

br-GWCv.title: Pole: long yellow ID, black code with a letter
br-GWCv.summary: Long yellow pole paint with a black code. Codes starting with a letter are found in Bahia and Pernambuco.

br-H1T8.title: Streetlight: zig-zag bent pole, yellow head
br-H1T8.summary: Lamps in Caxias do Sul (Rio Grande do Sul) usually have a zig-zag bent pole and a yellow head.

br-IcSJ.title: Road: hexagonal concrete tiles
br-IcSJ.summary: Hexagonal concrete tile roads exist across Brazil but are more common in Santa Catarina and Minas Gerais.

br-JTd6.title: Insulator: dark brown with grey base
br-JTd6.summary: Dark brown insulators with grey bases, almost only in Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

br-Jc9u.title: Coverage: island with white buggy, big rocks
br-Jc9u.summary: Fernando de Noronha, an island about 340 km north-east of Rio Grande do Norte, covered by a white buggy visible at the front. Plants like the nearest mainland, with large exposed rocks. Boat coverage too.

br-JkSy.title: Pole: spherical nests on top
br-JkSy.summary: Ball-shaped mud nests of the João-de-barro (oven bird) on top of poles, common across the south.

br-JlDz.title: Plants: Paraná pine with horizontal branches
br-JlDz.summary: Paraná pines have long horizontal branches with leaves only at the tips. They grow mainly in Paraná, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

br-MfEn.title: Pole: square yellow ID, three letters then numbers
br-MfEn.summary: In São Paulo state: a square yellow pole ID with three letters on top (the municipality, rarely visible), two digits, a black line and four digits.

br-N06x.title: Chevron: yellow arrows on black
br-N06x.summary: Chevrons are yellow on black, the opposite of most of South America (black on yellow).

br-NGXo.title: Streetlight: fancy, colourful lamp arm
br-NGXo.summary: In Ceará, lamps often have a fancy colourful arm, sometimes with the town name on it.

br-OGxZ.title: Plants: moriche palms
br-OGxZ.summary: Moriche palms: rounded fan leaves, dead bottom leaves hanging down. Most common in Roraima, Amazonas, Tocantins and Goiás, with random clusters further away. Also very common in Amazonian Colombia and Peru.

br-OfZt.title: Pole: electricity counters attached to poles
br-OfZt.summary: Electricity counters attached to poles are frequent in Cuiabá, Macapá and big cities in Pará. They can have one or several compartments.

br-OvbB.title: Landscape: big mountains with exposed rock
br-OvbB.summary: Large mountains with bare rock in Espírito Santo and the areas around it.

br-P82L.title: Pole: single support bar
br-P82L.summary: Poles with a single support are most common in Tocantins, Santa Catarina and Minas Gerais.

br-PA88.title: Pole: small yellow or orange plate on the pole
br-PA88.summary: A small yellow or orange plate fixed by thin metal or a zip tie, in Rio Grande do Norte and Pernambuco. It sits much higher on the pole in Pernambuco.

br-PCLq.title: Pavement: brown tiles, jagged or square
br-PCLq.summary: Brown tiled pavements, jagged and random or square, in Rio Grande do Sul and sometimes Santa Catarina.

br-PvkL.title: Pole: support bars linking crossbar to pole
br-PvkL.summary: Supports link the crossbar to the pole. How often depends on the state, and they are notably rare in the Northeast. Only works on poles with a crossbar.

br-UEBs.title: Insulator: lollipop on a rod
br-UEBs.summary: Round or cone insulators on a rod above the bar. Very common in Rio Grande do Norte, Paraíba and Pernambuco, rarer in Sergipe.

br-UO4B.title: Pole: street name painted on junction poles
br-UO4B.summary: In Paraná, utility poles at junctions are sometimes painted with the street name. Sometimes also in Santa Catarina or Rio Grande do Sul where ladder poles exist.

br-VBQt.title: Pole: zigzag top bar on a flat crossbar
br-VBQt.summary: A zigzag top bar on a flat crossbar, only in Ceará and Roraima. The pole is usually much bigger than normal.

br-WTWV.title: Streetlight: orange lamp heads
br-WTWV.summary: Lamp heads in Belém (Pará) are often orange.

br-X2iV.title: Pole: wooden poles in some states
br-X2iV.summary: Wooden poles are most common in Rio Grande do Sul, Roraima, Amazonas and Rio de Janeiro.

br-X9sq.title: Plants: carnaúba palms
br-X9sq.summary: Carnaúba palms: short strong fan leaves, trunk smooth at the top and spiky at the bottom. Common in Ceará, Piauí and Rio Grande do Norte, and around Xique-Xique in Bahia.

br-XAyk.title: Houses: concrete trash baskets
br-XAyk.summary: Trash baskets outside houses are usually metal, but in Acre and Rondônia they are more often concrete.

br-XPWf.title: Streetlight: lamp colour depends on the town
br-XPWf.summary: In Roraima, lamp colour depends on the town: Boa Vista, Normandia and Mucajaí red; Rorainópolis blue; Pacaraima and Iracema green; Caracaraí yellow.

br-XgcO.title: Insulator: white mushroom-shaped
br-XgcO.summary: White mushroom-shaped insulators are found in Bahia and rarely in Brasília.

br-XwFc.title: Road: cobbles of random sizes
br-XwFc.summary: Cobblestone roads with random-sized stones are most common in south-east Rio Grande do Sul and in Minas Gerais.

br-YM9a.title: Pole: ladder-like rectangular concrete
br-YM9a.summary: The most common poles are rectangular with long segments running through the bottom like a ladder, and small holes near the top. Paraguay uses similar poles.

br-YNbb.title: Coverage: mostly the eastern half
br-YNbb.summary: Most coverage is in the eastern half, with very little in the Amazon. Learn where western roads are so you do not guess hundreds of km from the nearest road.

br-aO5N.title: Pole: lamp arm attached directly to the pole
br-aO5N.summary: In Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Pará, Amapá, Rio Grande do Norte, Pernambuco and Santa Catarina, the lamp arm is attached directly to the pole instead of by a plate (more common elsewhere).

br-aYGO.title: Landscape: small grass hills, road rides over them
br-aYGO.summary: In Acre: small grassy hills with few trees, and roads that go over the hills instead of around them. A similar landscape exists near Marabá, Pará.

br-avhC.title: Route marker: two-letter state codes
br-avhC.summary: Each state has a two-letter code (SP, BA...), shown mainly in state road numbers on kilometre markers. It also shows on the map when you zoom out.

br-bnN1.title: Google car: low small camera, big round blur
br-bnN1.summary: Some Gen 4 coverage uses a camera mounted lower, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. Only Brazil, Peru and Argentina have it in South America.

br-cZMu.title: Landscape: dry soil, shrubs and succulents
br-cZMu.summary: The Northeast has dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga). In rainy-season coverage the shrubs can look deceptively green.

br-ctHo.title: Coverage: sand dunes with pools, white truck black bed
br-ctHo.summary: Lençóis Maranhenses National Park (Maranhão): sand dunes with pools of water, covered by a walker and a white truck with a black bed. Scenery ranges from beach to sandy wetland.

br-dEAg.title: Plants: macaw palms
br-dEAg.summary: Macaw palms: thin leaves, often a spear-shaped top. Very common around Mato Grosso do Sul, northern Tocantins and Belo Horizonte. One tree is a weak clue, several are better. Queen palms look similar but have fewer, less dense leaves.

br-dpxG.title: Sign: backs of road signs painted black
br-dpxG.summary: Most road signs have their backs painted black. Also common in Paraguay.

br-e3Yr.title: Route marker: blue with road number and km
br-e3Yr.summary: Blue markers show the road number and kilometre. The first two letters of a state road number are the state code (SP, MG...), except roads starting BR.

br-ejN1.title: Landscape: rolling grassy hills
br-ejN1.summary: Rolling grassy hills are common in Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo.

br-fnGk.title: Road: red brick roads
br-fnGk.summary: Some roads in Acre are made of red brick.

br-gsKs.title: Streetlight: light green lamps, many meters per pole
br-gsKs.summary: Lamps in Cuiabá (Mato Grosso) are usually light green, and poles often carry many electricity meters, sometimes 6 to 12.

br-iILP.title: Plants: sugarcane
br-iILP.summary: Sugarcane is by far most common in São Paulo, and common in Paraná, Mato Grosso do Sul and the coastal Northeast states.

br-iKjV.title: Pole: long yellow paint ID starting with a number
br-iKjV.summary: In Goiás: long yellow pole paint with a black code that always starts with a number. A rarer yellow-on-black ID, paint or plate, also exists there.

br-ipTk.title: Plants: very tall grass in the centre
br-ipTk.summary: Very tall grass is often seen in the centre, most of all in Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia and Minas Gerais.

br-j038.title: Plants: açaí palms
br-j038.summary: Açaí palms have drooping leaflets and unusually thin trunks. Most are near Belém, spread across the Amazon. Similar subspecies rarely grow along the coast from Santa Catarina to Bahia.

br-kO6H.title: Pole: small beige plate built into the pole
br-kO6H.summary: Most poles in Maranhão have a small beige numbered plate built into the pole. Rarer in Pará and Piauí.

br-kfSE.title: Houses: European-looking, vaguely German
br-kfSE.summary: Buildings in the southern states, mainly Santa Catarina, often have a European, vaguely German style.

br-kmTs.title: Road: red gravel along the roadside
br-kmTs.summary: Many roads in Piauí have red gravel beside the road, above the tarmac shoulder or on roads with kerbs. It can appear elsewhere, so use with caution.

br-kq8r.title: Landscape: flat wetland on the far-south coast
br-kq8r.summary: The coast of Rio Grande do Sul is flat wetland, which is rare in Brazil.

br-l5MR.title: Google car: blue, white with blue stripe, or white
br-l5MR.summary: Newer Gen 4 cars show the front and come in three looks: blue, white with a blue stripe, or plain white.

br-lm-55144.title: Plants: queen palms
br-lm-55144.summary: Queen palms: leaf stems point up the trunk then bow down. Native to South America, in Brazil mainly along the coast from Rio de Janeiro to Porto Alegre. Also Florida and eastern Australia.

br-lm-55146.title: Plants: pine trees in the south
br-lm-55146.summary: Pines are common in the south and rarely found north of Belo Horizonte.

br-lm-55147.title: Crops: cotton
br-lm-55147.summary: 73% of cotton is grown in Mato Grosso and 20% on the western border of Bahia. Minor areas: western Minas Gerais, southern Goiás, northern Mato Grosso do Sul.

br-lm-624864.title: Insulator: very long type of the six-ridge kind
br-lm-624864.summary: A sub-type of the six-plus ridge insulator, common in Pará, Paraná, Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul. The longer it looks, the more those states.

br-lm-624984.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-624986.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-624987.title: Insulator: five ridges
br-lm-624987.summary: Insulators with five ridges are very common in São Paulo.

br-lm-624988.title: Plants: Paraguay palm (not macaw palm)
br-lm-624988.summary: Often mistaken for macaw palm, but the trunk is smoother and the crown denser and rounder. It occurs closer to Paraguay than the macaw palm does.

br-lm-624989.title: Plants: juçara palm (not açaí)
br-lm-624989.summary: Closely related to açaí. Açaí grows in the flat north; juçara in the mountainous south-east, from Espírito Santo down to Rio Grande do Sul. Juçara has thinner leaves and grows with more space between plants.

br-lm-624990.title: Landscape: high coastal mountain range
br-lm-624990.summary: The Serra do Mar is a high range near the coast from Paraná to northern Rio Grande do Sul. A high-altitude road on the mountains, not in the valleys, is likely here.

br-lm-624991.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-625002.title: Insulator: round-shaped type, rare
br-lm-625002.summary: A rare insulator found mostly in Paraíba, Paraná, São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro. Unlike the lollipop insulator, its ridges differ in size.

br-lm-6335.title: Insulator: thin-stem cone or round shape
br-lm-6335.summary: In Rio Grande do Norte, Paraíba and Pernambuco: two insulators on thin stems, a cone thinning downward, and a rounded one whose bottom ridge is much smaller. Do not confuse with a three-equal-ridge type.

br-lm-656.title: Pole: small black square on a ladder pole
br-lm-656.summary: In Paraná, a small black square sits low on the flat side of ladder poles. Other states have unpainted indents or white dots, but black means Paraná. Not seeing it proves nothing; mostly newer poles.

br-lm-657.title: Pole: QR code sticker on almost every pole
br-lm-657.summary: In a small area just east of Belo Horizonte (Minas Gerais), almost every pole has a QR code sticker, found nowhere else.

br-lm-7498.title: Streetlight: plain white fancy lamp
br-lm-7498.summary: "Fancy lamps" are unique to north-west Paraná. This plain white one with no painted pattern is unique to Loanda.

br-lm-7499.title: Streetlight: fancy lamp, close to the next one
br-lm-7499.summary: Fancy lamp unique to Cidade Gaúcha (Paraná), very similar to the Campo Mourão one.

br-lm-7500.title: Streetlight: fancy lamp of the neighbour town
br-lm-7500.summary: Fancy lamp unique to Campo Mourão (Paraná), very similar to the Cidade Gaúcha one.

br-lm-7501.title: Streetlight: fancy lamp with yellow support
br-lm-7501.summary: Fancy lamp with a yellow support, unique to Goioerê (Paraná). Yellow supports are rarer in newer coverage.

br-lm-7502.title: Streetlight: fancy lamp, like the other town
br-lm-7502.summary: Fancy lamp unique to Umuarama (Paraná), strikingly similar to the Cidade Gaúcha one.

br-lm-7503.title: Streetlight: fancy lamp, unusual shape
br-lm-7503.summary: Fancy lamp with a uniquely shaped body, unique to Umuarama (Paraná).

br-lm-7504.title: Streetlight: tiny lamp
br-lm-7504.summary: "Tiny lamps" are unique to north-west Paraná. This one is unique to Loanda.

br-lm-7508.title: Pole: tiny black paint ID on bigger poles
br-lm-7508.summary: In Paraná, a tiny black paint ID is rarely found on larger poles. Worth a quick scan, especially in cities.

br-lm-7510.title: Streetlight: tiny lamp, sixth version
br-lm-7510.summary: Tiny lamp unique to Cruzeiro do Oeste (Paraná).

br-lm-7513.title: Pole: black ID paint, decimal point means one city
br-lm-7513.summary: Black pole IDs are common in Paraná except in Curitiba. A decimal point in the number means Londrina.

br-lm-7514.title: Pole: little blue painted numbers
br-lm-7514.summary: Londrina (Paraná) sometimes has little blue numbers painted on poles.

br-lm-7515.title: Pole: tiny black ID with white number and arrow
br-lm-7515.summary: A tiny black paint ID with a white number and a triangular arrow, unique to Cascavel (Paraná).

br-lm-7516.title: Streetlight: blue lamp
br-lm-7516.summary: Cascavel (Paraná) uses this blue lamp, but it is very rare in newer coverage.

br-lm-7517.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7518.title: Electric boxes: open or trashed
br-lm-7518.summary: Open or trashed electricity boxes are frequent in Marabá and Santarém (Pará).

br-lm-7519.title: Electric boxes: yellow skull stickers
br-lm-7519.summary: Yellow skull stickers are common on electricity boxes in Marabá (Pará).

br-lm-7520.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7521.title: Pole: city ID with holes on the sides
br-lm-7521.summary: A city pole ID distinct for the holes on its sides, from Imperatriz (Maranhão).

br-lm-7522.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7523.title: Streetlight: a cute lamp
br-lm-7523.summary: A cute little lamp unique to Gurupi (Tocantins).

br-lm-7524.title: Pole: large ID plate
br-lm-7524.summary: A rather large pole ID is common in Betim (Minas Gerais).

br-lm-7525.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7526.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7527.title: Pole: IDs by first digit
br-lm-7527.summary: In Minas Gerais: pole IDs starting 0 or 1 mean Belo Horizonte; starting 2 or 3 (sometimes 1) mean Uberaba. They do not appear in other cities there.

br-lm-7528.title: Streetlight: zig-zag lamp arm
br-lm-7528.summary: This zig-zag lamp arm is unique to Caxias do Sul (Rio Grande do Sul).

br-lm-7529.title: Road: stone road markings
br-lm-7529.summary: Stone road markings are unique to Caxias do Sul (Rio Grande do Sul).

br-lm-7530.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7531.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7547.title: Streetlight: two-part lamp enveloping the light
br-lm-7547.summary: A two-part lamp, most common in Minas Gerais and Goiás. This variant with both parts around the lamp is more common in Minas Gerais. Also in Rio Grande do Norte and Rio Grande do Sul, the Federal District, and rarely Pará, Mato Grosso and Rondônia.

br-lm-7548.title: Streetlight: two-part lamp, pole visible underneath
br-lm-7548.summary: A two-part lamp with the pole visible underneath, more common in Goiás. Otherwise as the Minas Gerais variant: also in Rio Grande do Norte, Rio Grande do Sul and the Federal District.

br-lm-7550.title: Pole: anything odd about the pole
br-lm-7550.summary: When something out of the ordinary is going on with a pole, it is Rio de Janeiro.

br-lm-7560.title: Pole: yellow plate embedded in the pole
br-lm-7560.summary: A yellow plate set into the pole, mainly in Maranhão, spilling into Pará and Piauí.

br-lm-7561.title: Pole: statewide ID style in the north
br-lm-7561.summary: Pará uses its own statewide pole ID style.

br-lm-7562.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7564.title: Pole: electricity company name engraved
br-lm-7564.summary: Electricity company names are engraved on poles and often match state names: CELPA is Pará, COSERN is Rio Grande do Norte, COELCE is Ceará.

br-lm-7565.title: Pole: ID with a numbered square above
br-lm-7565.summary: A two-section ID whose upper part is a square with a number, in Pernambuco.

br-lm-7572.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7574.title: Streetlight: short arm and top light
br-lm-7574.summary: A lamp with a short arm and a top light, specific to Tocantins.

br-lm-7575.title: Streetlight: blue lamp, top light, underside pattern
br-lm-7575.summary: A blue lamp with a top light and a unique underside pattern, specific to Tocantins.

br-lm-7576.title: Streetlight: long blue lamp with top light
br-lm-7576.summary: A long blue lamp with a top light and a unique underside pattern, specific to Tocantins.

br-lm-7583.title: Insulator: six or more ridges
br-lm-7583.summary: Insulators with six or more ridges: common in Bahia, Tocantins, Maranhão, Pará, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Paraná and Santa Catarina; uncommon in Acre, Rondônia, Amapá, Piauí, Goiás, São Paulo and Rio Grande do Sul; rare in Rio Grande do Norte and Rio de Janeiro.

br-lm-7600.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7601.title: Road: black and white striped kerbs
br-lm-7601.summary: Black and white striped kerbs are common in Boa Vista (Roraima).

br-lm-7602.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7603.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7604.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7605.title: Pole: ID above the lamp attachment
br-lm-7605.summary: In Manaus, pole IDs are usually above where the lamp attaches.

br-lm-7606.title: Streetlight: green lamps in three big cities
br-lm-7606.summary: Green lamps appear in three large cities: Cuiabá, Manaus and Vitória.

br-lm-7607.title: Road: empty flat roads and roundabouts
br-lm-7607.summary: Roundabouts and odd road layouts that are mostly empty and perfectly flat are common in Palmas (Tocantins).

br-lm-7608.title: Sign: all street signs corroded
br-lm-7608.summary: All the street signs in Palmas (Tocantins) are corroded.

br-lm-7609.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7610.title: Coverage: hazy sky
br-lm-7610.summary: Hazy skies are very common in Porto Velho (Rondônia).

br-lm-7612.title: Sign: yellow stick with sign attached
br-lm-7612.summary: A yellow stick, often with a sign attached, is common in Rio Branco (Acre).

br-lm-7613.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7615.title: Streetlight: pointy front, blue or yellow top light
br-lm-7615.summary: A lamp head with a pointy front and a blue or yellow top light.

br-lm-7616.title: Pole: rare ID of one north-eastern city
br-lm-7616.summary: A rare pole ID specific to São Luís (Maranhão). The embedded Maranhão IDs are more common.

br-lm-7622.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7623.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7624.title: Pole: two ID types in a north-eastern city
br-lm-7624.summary: Two kinds of ID are common in Fortaleza (Ceará).

br-lm-7625.title: Pole: red sticker below the lamp
br-lm-7625.summary: A red sticker below the lamp is unique to Fortaleza (Ceará).

br-lm-7626.title: Streetlight: aerodynamic lamp heads
br-lm-7626.summary: Streamlined lamp heads are common in Fortaleza (Ceará).

br-lm-7627.title: Pavement: distinct stone sidewalks and driveways
br-lm-7627.summary: Distinct stone sidewalks and driveways in João Pessoa (Paraíba).

br-lm-7628.title: Road lines: white centre lines, rare yellow dashes
br-lm-7628.summary: White centre lines are very common in João Pessoa (Paraíba); yellow dashed lines are rare.

br-lm-7629.title: Pole: ladder poles with holes
br-lm-7629.summary: Ladder poles with holes are very common in João Pessoa (Paraíba), though not unique to it.

br-lm-7630.title: Pole: uncommon ID unique to one state
br-lm-7630.summary: An uncommon pole ID unique to Paraíba, most common in the capital João Pessoa.

br-lm-7631.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7632.title: Streetlight: long post, bent arm, dot at bottom
br-lm-7632.summary: Long posts with a bent top arm and a yellow or grey dot at the bottom.

br-lm-7633.title: Pole: two rare IDs of one city
br-lm-7633.summary: Two rare pole IDs unique to Maceió (Alagoas).

br-lm-7634.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7635.title: Pole: internet ads on poles
br-lm-7635.summary: Internet ads attached to poles are very common in Natal (Rio Grande do Norte). Mnemonic: Internatal.

br-lm-7636.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7637.title: Pole: ID unique to one big north-eastern city
br-lm-7637.summary: A pole ID unique to Recife (Pernambuco). It can be faded or other colours; the shape matters.

br-lm-7638.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7639.title: Pavement: black and white broken tile pattern
br-lm-7639.summary: A unique sidewalk of black and white broken tiles in Salvador (Bahia); other patterns exist too.

br-lm-7640.title: Bollard: black and yellow
br-lm-7640.summary: Black and yellow bollards of different kinds are common in Salvador (Bahia).

br-lm-7641.title: Streetlight: long yellow ID on the lamp arm
br-lm-7641.summary: A long yellow ID on the lamp arm, which can be very hard to spot.

br-lm-7642.title: Pole: well-known urban ID in a north-eastern city
br-lm-7642.summary: Very common in Teresina (Piauí), one of the best-known urban Brazil clues.

br-lm-7647.title: Pole: right-angle top bars
br-lm-7647.summary: Right-angle top bars are common in Brasília.

br-lm-7648.title: Pole: few poles, curved lamp posts instead
br-lm-7648.summary: A suspicious lack of poles, with curved lamp posts instead, points to Brasília.

br-lm-7649.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7650.title: Road lines: yellow dashed lines and speedbumps
br-lm-7650.summary: Yellow dashed lines and speedbumps are very common in Brasília, but not unique to it.

br-lm-7651.title: Sign: blue pole-wrapped signs
br-lm-7651.summary: Blue street signs wrapped around poles, unique to Campo Grande (Mato Grosso do Sul).

br-lm-7652.title: Sign: state flags in cities
br-lm-7652.summary: In urban areas state flags might show up, which can sometimes pay off.

br-lm-7653.title: Pole: neon-yellow vertical IDs
br-lm-7653.summary: Neon-yellow vertical pole IDs in Campo Grande (Mato Grosso do Sul) and Vitória (Espírito Santo). Not the larger horizontal ones of São Paulo.

br-lm-7655.title: Streetlight: small blue item hanging from arm
br-lm-7655.summary: A small blue item hanging from the lamp arm: in Cuiabá (bent arm attached to the pole) and in Ribeirão Preto and São Paulo (normal arm).

br-lm-7656.title: Landscape: steep rolling hills, no trees, dirt road
br-lm-7656.summary: In Roraima: a windy green dirt road over rolling hills with no trees. This one is thinner and steeper than the road south of Uiramutã.

br-lm-7658.title: Pole: ID style of one south-eastern state
br-lm-7658.summary: These pole IDs are specific to Minas Gerais. Starting with 0 or 1 means Belo Horizonte.

br-lm-7659.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7660.title: Streetlight: curvy arm, big head
br-lm-7660.summary: A curvy lamp arm with a usually big head.

br-lm-7661.title: Taxi: completely yellow
br-lm-7661.summary: Taxis in Rio de Janeiro are completely yellow.

br-lm-7662.title: Streetlight: straight neck, tight top bend
br-lm-7662.summary: A lamp with a long straight neck, a tight bend at the top and a usually thin head.

br-lm-7663.title: Streetlight: connector pointing downwards
br-lm-7663.summary: A clue for São Paulo, only when the connector points downwards; upward connectors are generic.

br-lm-7665.title: Pole: neon-yellow horizontal ID
br-lm-7665.summary: Neon-yellow horizontal pole IDs, specific to São Paulo. Campo Grande and Vitória have smaller vertical ones.

br-lm-7666.title: Sign: unique street sign design
br-lm-7666.summary: A unique street sign design in Vitória (Espírito Santo).

br-lm-7667.title: Pavement: small-tile red tactile paving
br-lm-7667.summary: Red tactile paving with small tiles and round bumps is very common in Vitória (Espírito Santo). Florianópolis has large-tile red paving.

br-lm-7668.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7669.title: Electric boxes: metal box between plastic ones
br-lm-7669.summary: A metal electricity box sandwiched between plastic ones is very common in Vitória (Espírito Santo).

br-lm-7671.title: Road: grass verges between sidewalk and road
br-lm-7671.summary: Grass verges between sidewalk and road are common in Curitiba (Paraná).

br-lm-7672.title: Pavement: chessboard-pattern sidewalks
br-lm-7672.summary: Chessboard-pattern sidewalks are common in Curitiba (Paraná).

br-lm-7673.title: Road lines: yellow edge lines on city roads
br-lm-7673.summary: Yellow edge lines on urban roads are very common in Curitiba (Paraná).

br-lm-7674.title: Pole: WiFi-password-like ID codes
br-lm-7674.summary: Pole IDs with codes like WiFi passwords (mixed digits, upper and lowercase letters) mean Curitiba (Paraná).

br-lm-7675.hide: too vague; same topic as br-lm-7672

br-lm-7676.title: Pole: street signs attached to poles
br-lm-7676.summary: Some poles in Curitiba have street signs attached, though regular generic signs are also used.

br-lm-7677.title: Streetlight: red lamps like the northern city ones
br-lm-7677.summary: Red lamps like those of Belém, found in the Ipiranga neighbourhood of Florianópolis (Santa Catarina).

br-lm-7678.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7680.title: Pole: wooden poles in a green, tidy city
br-lm-7680.summary: Porto Alegre (Rio Grande do Sul) is greener, cleaner and roomier than other cities, so the common wooden poles look out of place.

br-lm-7682.hide: no learnable content (place name or caption only)

br-lm-7683.title: Coverage: camera glitch in the far south-west
br-lm-7683.summary: Older Gen 3 coverage in north-west Rio Grande do Sul has a particular camera glitch.

br-lm-7684.title: Pavement: black and white stone patterns
br-lm-7684.summary: Campinas (São Paulo) is known for artistic black and white stone patterns on its sidewalks.

br-lm-7685.title: Sign: colourful thick signposts
br-lm-7685.summary: Colourful, thick signposts found in several cities of São Paulo state.

br-lm-7691.title: Road: divided, one side asphalt, the other concrete
br-lm-7691.summary: A divided road with asphalt in one direction and concrete in the other. No longer true for the whole road.

br-lm-7692.title: Pole: crossbar with no supports in the north-east
br-lm-7692.summary: Crossbars with no support bars are almost only in Piauí, Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte and Alagoas, frequent across the Northeast and in Rondônia and Roraima.

br-lm-7694.title: Road: front-blur on blue-striped car, areca palms
br-lm-7694.summary: Part of a road in Amapá: the slight front blur on the blue-striped car, a red car front, a north-west road angle and areca palms nearby.

br-lm-7695.title: Road: windy, steep cliffs, in the clouds
br-lm-7695.summary: A windy road in eastern Santa Catarina with steep mountains and cliffs, like driving in the clouds. It passes the Corvo Branco tourist cut.

br-lm-7696.title: Road: unique pavement and sand dunes
br-lm-7696.summary: A road east of Fortaleza (Ceará) with unique pavement and sand dunes alongside.

br-lm-7697.title: Coverage: flooded road
br-lm-7697.summary: Flooded coverage between Macau and Macauzinho in Rio Grande do Norte.

br-lm-7698.title: Road: uneven red stone pavement, corn fields
br-lm-7698.summary: A road west of Cascavel and south of Toledo (Paraná), by PR-585, with uneven red stone paving and corn fields.

br-lm-7699.title: Road: thin red gravel stripe
br-lm-7699.summary: A road with a thin red stripe of gravel, east of Teresina (Piauí).

br-lm-7700.title: Road: concrete with black tar behind lines
br-lm-7700.summary: A concrete road north of Rio de Janeiro city with black tar behind the road lines.

br-lm-7702.title: Road: very swampy, few trees, very red soil
br-lm-7702.summary: A very swampy road (PA-154) north-west of Belém (Pará), with very few trees and very red soil.

br-lm-7703.title: Road: smudge, blue-striped car, east-west, paved
br-lm-7703.summary: Part of BR-156 in Amapá: the only Amapá-blur road going east-west, and paved.

br-lm-7704.title: Road: Amazon trees, NW-SE angle, blue car front
br-lm-7704.summary: An Amazonian-looking road running north-west to south-east, always Gen 4 with the exposed blue car front.

br-lm-7705.title: Road: water south, wall north, three line types
br-lm-7705.summary: A road west of Rio de Janeiro city: water to the south, lines going double yellow, double broken yellow, single broken white, and a small wall to the north. Mountains show to the north.

br-lm-7706.title: Road: wide dirt, Amazon trees, no other cars
br-lm-7706.summary: A wide dirt road with Amazon trees and a blurred car, no other cars, the only east-west road in its area.

br-lm-7707.title: Road: Amazon look, SW-NE angle
br-lm-7707.summary: An Amazonian-looking road running south-west to north-east, with some overcast or flat stretches.

br-lm-7708.title: Road: red dirt stripes both sides, babassu palms
br-lm-7708.summary: A north-south road with a thick strip of red dirt on both sides and frequent babassu palms.

br-lm-7709.title: Road: swamp, pine trees, lagoon
br-lm-7709.summary: A south-east to north-west road with swampy land, pines and a lagoon.

br-lm-7710.title: Landscape: gentler rolling hills, no trees, dirt road
br-lm-7710.summary: In Roraima: a windy green dirt road over rolling hills with no trees. This one is wider and less steep than the road south of Uiramutã.

br-lm-7711.title: Road: Amazon look, east-west, mud stains
br-lm-7711.summary: A rainforest road running east-west slightly south, looking stained with mud.

br-lm-7712.title: Road lines: outer dashed lines
br-lm-7712.summary: Dashed outer lines can rarely be found in Rio Grande do Norte and other Northeast states.

br-lm-7713.title: Coverage: after a bushfire, outer dashed lines
br-lm-7713.summary: The road between Caicó (Rio Grande do Norte) and Santa Luzia (Paraíba) has post-bushfire coverage. The Paraíba part often has outer dashed lines.

br-lm-7714.title: Houses: red brick houses
br-lm-7714.summary: Red brick houses are more common in the Northeast.

br-lm-7715.title: Pole: yellow paint ID with only numbers
br-lm-7715.summary: Yellow pole paint like São Paulo's but all digits, found in Rio de Janeiro.

br-m0g3.title: Road: uneven mostly square stones, dark soil
br-m0g3.summary: Uneven, mostly square stone roads in western Rio Grande do Sul and western Santa Catarina, often with very dark soil. The same roads exist in Misiones, Argentina.

br-mIAJ.title: Pole: Γ-shaped with electricity boxes at the end
br-mIAJ.summary: Γ-shaped poles with electricity boxes at the end, most common in Rio de Janeiro and the cities Belém, Salvador, Fortaleza and Maceió. A shorter-bar version is only in Belém.

br-n1ox.title: Coverage: rifts in older camera
br-n1ox.summary: Rifts (stitching glitches) are often seen in older Gen 3 coverage in Alagoas.

br-nX3d.title: Language: Portuguese (-ão, lh, nh)
br-nX3d.summary: Portuguese, not Spanish. Look for -ão instead of -ón, lh/ch instead of ll, and nh instead of ñ.

br-nqxg.title: Insulator: long and thin
br-nqxg.summary: Uniquely long, thin insulators in Ceará, and rarely in Goiás.

br-oNlC.title: Landscape: red soil
br-oNlC.summary: Soil in most of Brazil is distinctly red, from light pink around Mato Grosso to deep maroon near the Paraná river. Usually not red in the Northeast or most of Rio Grande do Sul. Paraguay and Misiones (Argentina) have deep red soil too.

br-oot8.title: Houses: blue water tanks on roofs
br-oot8.summary: Blue water tanks (Fortlev) often sit on roofs.

br-otjB.title: Phone numbers: two-digit area codes
br-otjB.summary: Area codes in brackets or as a separate number. Without them, landlines have 8 digits and mobiles 9. Codes are grouped by first digit, and codes ending in 1 are around big cities and capitals.

br-qiaH.title: Houses: wooden on stilts
br-qiaH.summary: Wooden houses on stilts are very common in Acre, and rarer in low-lying Amazonas and Pará.

br-r5UP.title: Pole: top insulator plus alternating side ones
br-r5UP.summary: One insulator on top and horizontal ones alternating below, in Mato Grosso and southern Acre. Very rare in Rio Grande do Sul.

br-rQrQ.title: Landscape: open grass plains, big distant mountains
br-rQrQ.summary: In Roraima: open grassy plains with large distant mountains behind, and thin grass growing in bunches. Sometimes the road goes through the mountains.

br-rdVZ.title: Houses: orange tiled roofs
br-rdVZ.summary: Many houses have orange tiled roofs.

br-s2pM.title: Streetlight: no arm, colourful plastic or fancy
br-s2pM.summary: In northern Paraná, some city lamps have no arm, either colourful plastic and industrial or fancy and ornate. Both are most common in north-west Paraná.

br-sjAl.title: Sign: postcodes on street signs
br-sjAl.summary: Postcodes (CEP) on street signs: the first two digits point to a state or several states, numbered anti-clockwise from São Paulo to Rio Grande do Sul.

br-u4vX.title: Pole: lopsided crossbar with no supports
br-u4vX.summary: A lopsided crossbar with no supports, only in Ceará and Rondônia. Usually concrete in Ceará; Rondônia has a rarer metal version.

br-vAH9.title: Insulator: brown mushroom-shaped
br-vAH9.summary: Brown mushroom-shaped insulators are only found in Pernambuco.

br-vMha.title: Road: rollercoaster road riding the hills
br-vMha.summary: Road 364 through Acre: a rollercoaster road that rides over the hills instead of around them, usually with no traffic, mostly with the blue Gen 4 car.

br-vUCq.title: Landscape: lush green fields, hilly or flat
br-vUCq.summary: In Rio Grande do Sul: lush green fields, hilly or flat. The south can look like Uruguay.

differs.how: Southern areas look similar to Uruguay

br-wqhj.title: Pole: white with blue and red stripes
br-wqhj.summary: Poles on Santa Catarina Island (Florianópolis) are painted white with blue and red stripes.

br-xH0Y.title: Plants: babassu palms
br-xH0Y.summary: Babassu palms: long robust leaves of many leaflets, trunk short or tall. Found throughout the Amazon, more rarely down the east coast.

br-xjGP.title: Plants: soybeans
br-xjGP.summary: Small leafy soybean plants, mostly grown in Mato Grosso, Paraná and Goiás.

br-y0J7.title: Google car: white, coiled stubby antenna (Gen 3)
br-y0J7.summary: In older Gen 3 coverage (blurrier, softer colours): a white car with a stubby antenna wrapped in a diagonal coil, or a white car with no antenna, often with no car visible at all. The coiled antenna also appears in Ecuador, Colombia and Mexico.

br-yPwJ.title: Plants: long-stemmed leafy plant in the north-east
br-yPwJ.summary: A plant with long stems and upward leaves, very common in Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte and Paraíba. In the dry season the long bare stems still show.

br-ySa0.title: Pole: round concrete poles in the south
br-ySa0.summary: Besides ladder poles, round concrete poles are common in the south, especially São Paulo. Big-city centres often have round poles anywhere.

br-z5v9.title: Pole: horizontal insulators
br-z5v9.summary: Horizontal insulators are very common in Pará, less so in Mato Grosso, and rare in Acre, Amapá, Tocantins, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

br-zJtI.title: Route marker: phone numbers under km markers
br-zJtI.summary: In São Paulo, phone numbers can sometimes be seen under kilometre markers.

br-zZ1A.title: Pole: black paint with yellow or white text
br-zZ1A.summary: In Paraná, pole IDs are black paint with yellow or white text.

br-zcD0.title: Streetlight: lamp in two parts
br-zcD0.summary: Two-part lamps are common in Minas Gerais and Goiás, and also found in Rio Grande do Norte, Ceará, Rio Grande do Sul and the Federal District.
